plan.title: refactor(agents-md): Phase 2 Wave 3a — evict Content packs / Skills / Codebase MAP from managed section

narratives.Description: Pointer-out Content packs, Skills, and Codebase MAP cards from content/templates/agents-entry.md to on-demand docs; keep !/⊗ one-liners. ~2.0–2.5 KB toward managed ≤8192 under epic #2491.
narratives.UserStory: As a framework maintainer, I want discovery and orientation prose out of always-on AGENTS.md, so that consumers load less text while agents still find packs, skills, and MAP guidance on demand.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1) Rewrite Content packs, Skills, and Codebase MAP sections in content/templates/agents-entry.md to pointer-thin !/⊗ lines targeting packs:slice, REFERENCES.md Skills Index, and codebase:map / plan.architecture.codeStructure. 2) Relocate any needed prose into content/commands.md or REFERENCES.md pointers; update packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/agents_entry_contract.test.ts markers (retire full-text, pointer-sufficient). 3) Run task agents:refresh; re-seed absoluteMaxBytes (and line ratchet if needed) in xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json. 4) CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] Closes #2501 Refs #2491. Verify: pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/agents_entry_contract.test.ts; task verify:agents-md-budget; task check --allow-over-cap.
narratives.Overview: Conflict group agents-entry-phase2 — serialize ahead of #2502 Wave 3b.

narrative.Acceptance: Given agents-entry, when Content packs / Skills / Codebase MAP are read, then they are pointer-thin with no multi-bullet discovery walkthroughs always-on.
Given marker updates, when agents_entry_contract tests run, then pointer-sufficient rules pass and retired full-text markers are gone.
Given the byte drop, when agents:refresh and verify:agents-md-budget run, then AGENTS.md matches and absoluteMaxBytes is re-seeded downward.
Given merge, when PR lands, then CHANGELOG cites Closes #2501 Refs #2491.

expected_outputs: pointer-thin Content packs / Skills / Codebase MAP sections
